panelOverviewHint: Checks originate from the panel server. Browse target server status and history by type.
panelSourceHint: The panel originates checks; node servers provide heartbeats and target services.
checkIntro_all: Select a check type to learn about its protocol and view results.
checkIntro_tcp: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) provides a connection-oriented, reliable, ordered byte stream using acknowledgements and retransmissions. TCP checks measure whether a target port accepts a connection and how long it takes.
checkIntro_udp: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) sends connectionless datagrams without guaranteeing delivery or ordering. It is used by DNS and real-time media applications. UDP checks send a payload and wait for a reply.
checkIntro_ping: ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) carries error and control information for IP networks. Ping uses echo requests and replies to measure round-trip latency and loss; firewall policies can affect replies.
checkIntro_http: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) exchanges web and API resources through requests and responses. HTTPS protects HTTP with TLS and authenticates the server. These checks examine response status, content, timing and certificates.
checkIntro_dns: DNS (Domain Name System) is a distributed naming system for records such as IP addresses and mail servers. Traditional queries use UDP or TCP port 53. DNS checks inspect answers and query time.
checkIntro_mtr: MTR combines route tracing and repeated probes to report replies, latency and loss along a path. It is a diagnostic tool, not a separate protocol; router reply limits can affect its output.
checkIntro_traceroute: Traceroute infers a route by increasing the IP time-to-live (TTL) and examining replies. It is a diagnostic tool, not a separate protocol, and can use UDP, ICMP or TCP probes.
udpHint: A successful send is not a health check. A response is required; no response does not prove the port is closed.
udpExpected: Response contains (same encoding; blank accepts any non-empty reply)
